corpus_aggregate.note: Stages 1+2 from prior validation (47+38=85 claims); Stages 3-6 scored here (52+54+56+58=220 claims). Total: 305.
corpus_aggregate.note_on_unique_sources: Counted by distinct publication/domain family. Government filings (10-K, 6-K, S-1, ASX) counted individually per company. Same aggregator domain (GlobeNewswire for market research press releases) counted per underlying firm. Same-stage URL reuse across value-chain and pain-points files counted once. Estimate: 40-50 High-quality primary sources; 60-70 secondary/trade; 25-30 auto-Low aggregator/vendor-self; 20-25 company press releases.
corpus_aggregate.note_on_diversity: 178 unique sources / ~307 total citation instances ≈ 0.58. Just below the 0.60 target, driven by TT Club/BSI 2024 Cargo Theft Report being cited 14+ times across Stages 3-6 (legitimate given its scope) and CargoNet/Verisk cited 10+ times. Same-source over-reliance is defensible for the TT Club/CargoNet sources given their authoritative status in cargo crime data.

Cargo up 1.6% YoY. Asia/Pacific 35.15% share confirmed. PDF was blocked on automated fetch but IUMI press release and IIMS.org.uk secondary confirm all figures.

factual_cross_checks.claim: Swiss Re Sigma $740B APAC protection gap (attributed to Peak Re in Stage 6)
factual_cross_checks.notes: My search found Peak Re's protection gap figure for emerging Asia in 2023 is $441B (Reinsurance News citing Peak Re), not $740B. The draft attributes this to 'Peak Re analysis' via Intelligent Insurer. Swiss Re Sigma 3/2024 shows global total protection gap of $1.83T. A $740B APAC-only figure would represent 40% of global total, which appears implausibly large. Most likely error: (a) confusion between a broader Peak Re metric including mortality/health gap, (b) a different publication year's figure, or (c) misattribution of a different organization's number. The underlying structural argument (material underinsurance in emerging Asia) is directionally sound; the specific $740B figure should be corrected to $441B or sourced more precisely. RECOMMEND: flag for attended fetch of the Peak Re primary PDF before publication.

Recommend: replace 303% with '576 events in 2023 vs. 66/year historical average' which is directly sourced and more striking.

gate_reasoning: Corpus aggregate Low-confidence rate of 27.9% (85 of 305 scored claims) places this run within the 20-30% ship-with-flag band. Three factors drive the flag beyond the Low-confidence rate alone. First, the $740B APAC protection gap figure in Stage 6 PP6.3 is a probable factual error: available primary research places Peak Re's emerging Asia protection gap at $441B, not $740B, and the $740B figure cannot be cross-validated from accessible sources. This figure appears in a structurally important section (the market-gap argument for SEA cargo insurance) and should be corrected before the corpus is used in investor or client-facing materials. Second, the CargoNet +303% fictitious pickups figure cited in Stages 5 and 6 does not match any CargoNet published annual aggregate; the correct characterization (576 events in 2023 vs. 66/year historical average) is more accurate and more powerful, and should replace the 303% figure. Third, the McKinsey 2024 '30% beyond Tier-1' figure — the single most-cited governance statistic in Stage 4 — is sourced from a paywalled article that blocked automated fetch; it is cross-confirmed directionally via secondary sources but not directly verified from the primary PDF. All three flags are correctable without re-running the research. The rest of the corpus is well-anchored: audited SEC/ASX/TSX filings cover 12+ named companies; government primary sources (FMCSA, MPA Singapore, DCSA, IUMI, ReCAAP, Maersk/IBM primary press releases) anchor the most important structural claims; the TradeLens, Vietnam data law, IUMI premiums, Nirvana/TMFF, and Malacca piracy statistics are all independently verified. The cross-stage data consistency is high — no contradictions found between stages for any number cited in multiple locations. Citation diversity at 0.58 is marginally below the 0.60 target but defensible given the nature of the sources (CargoNet and TT Club/BSI are the only credible primary cargo crime databases and their multi-stage citation is appropriate).
